extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (postdocs, early-stage investigators, faculty) seeking guidance on funding decisions and post-review steps
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for applicants on how funding decisions are made, what to do after peer review (contacting PO, JIT, overlapping applications, resubmission), and IC/FOA-specific rules that affect award outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile as basis for funding (CSR-reviewed applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since your application went to a CSR (vs NIA) panel, your percentile will be the basis of any funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your application was reviewed by CSR, the percentile (not just raw impact score) is typically the primary metric used by ICs to make funding decisions. Exceptions may apply for FOAs with set-aside funds or other special mechanisms. After you receive your summary statement, check with your PO for IC-specific interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOA / set-aside funds can override payline expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Because this is a PAS, there is a putative cap on the number of awards (based on the set-aside funds), so it will also depend on where NIA is in terms of spending this pot of money (if it is all spent, they are not obligated to fund you just because you are within the payline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FOAs with a fixed number of awards or set-aside funding, being at/within a payline does not guarantee an award. Investigate historical funding for that FOA and ask your PO how the set-aside is being spent this cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wait until the summary statement before contacting the PO
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical guidance is to ALWAYS wait until summary statement comes out. PO can’t say anything until then and it’s being considerate of their time & confidentiality issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not contact the PO immediately upon receiving a score; wait for the summary statement (pink sheets) so the PO can see reviewer concerns. Exceptions exist (e.g., if the PO is also your mentor or you have a prior relationship), but the general rule is to wait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated JIT notifications are routine and not a funding promise
rubrics_metrics.description: The Just-in-Time link appears in eRA Commons for all grant applications within 24 hours after the score is released. The NIH automatically issues an email requesting JIT for all applications with an impact score of 30 or less. Both the automatic link and the automated email should be ignored. The GMS or PO will email the PI directly if the IC intends to consider the application for an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat automated JIT links/emails as system behavior, not an indication of fundability. Only respond to a personalized JIT request from the Grants Management Specialist or Program Official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose pending/overlapping submissions in JIT and other support
rubrics_metrics.description: You would submit it as pending support and indicate that the application would be withdrawn if the A1 is awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responding to JIT or completing Other Support, disclose parallel/pending submissions and clearly state that you will withdraw overlapping applications if one is awarded. This is routine and required to avoid improper double-support.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDeA co-funding nominations come from the PO (PI requests not determinative)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your PO wants to nominate your application for IDeA co-funding, they do that on their own (your requesting consideration wouldn’t make a difference – ICs can only nominate a few applications, so they pick internally from among many eligible applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot reliably lobby for IDeA co-funding yourself; the PO or IC makes internal nominations. If nominated, the PO will inform you and next steps will follow (e.g., withdraw pending application if co-funding secured).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary IC assignment does not indicate funding interest
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS takes itself off any applications to which CSR assigns it as a secondary IC because they do not fund applications as secondary IC (and do not want to give PIs false hopes). Secondary IC funding is pretty rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that being listed as a secondary IC means that institute will or wants to fund your application. If you are curious about an institute's interest, ask the appropriate PO, but treat secondary assignment cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to shorten K99/K award period require PO approval and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: If your K99 is for 2 years, then you would want to talk with your PO about shortening it to 1 year. You will need to demonstrate that you can accomplish all the peer-reviewed training (described in the application) in a shorter time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any requested change in a career award’s duration or training plan should be discussed with the PO in advance and must show how the objectives will still be met in the shorter period; be prepared with a concrete plan and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending administrative review / long 'pending' periods are common
rubrics_metrics.description: The long Pending period is not unusual... The delay is not necessarily bad, since it’s faster for ICs to identify the applications that definitely won’t get awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not panic if eRA shows 'pending administrative review' for weeks or months. Contact the PO only if you need clarifying information (e.g., for planning), otherwise be patient — the GMS will contact you if they need documents or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve percent-effort overlap in JIT; delaying start date is an acceptable remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the investigators and myself will have over 100% effort if the grant is funded now. ... We explained and also adjusted the effort in April and May to avoid any potential overlap if the new project is funded. ... I think you could have just asked about delaying the start until May to avoid the overlap and effort problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed effort would exceed allowable commitments, respond in JIT by adjusting month-by-month effort, proposing a delayed start date, or otherwise resolving overlap; GMS will request clarification if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission (A1) can substantially improve a score
rubrics_metrics.description: It is very common to drop from even higher (even non-discussed) scores to within funding range from the A0 to A1, especially if the reviewer concerns are clear and make sense (ie, are easily addressed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address reviewer critiques directly in your A1. Discuss strategy with your PO after the summary statement; resubmission can move you into fundable range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate FOA-specific funding history and heed PO advice for borderline scores
rubrics_metrics.description: The single award for this PAR could reflect few applications in total or few competitive applications. The PO could have advised you to apply again because they want to keep that FOA alive ... or because you are close but they cannot advocate for funding at such a high percentile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a FOA has produced very few awards historically, treat borderline scores cautiously and consult your PO about resubmission vs alternate mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award 'we plan to fund' letters are not the Notice of Award (NOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: I was wondering whether you or other people have experience in receiving a letter from NIH, starting with 'The National… and we plan to fund your application. However, this letter does not take the place of the official Notice of Grant Award.' ... Would this mean I should just wait and expect an NOA very soon?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'we plan to fund' communication is preliminary. Expect administrative processing steps (JIT, GMS actions) and an official NOA (Notice of Award) later; timing can vary and a short delay between 'award prepared' and NOA issuance is normal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI status and extensions — check institute policy and COVID-related extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs fund ESI up to the 25th percentile, but NIDCR does not have a big budget, so they might stop their ESI funding at the 20th percentile or lower ... If my ESI ends in July do all July submission still count my ESI? I did submit an extension for my ESI due to covid ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESI paylines and how long ESI status is honored vary by IC. Check the institute’s guidelines and ask your PO about COVID-era extensions or how ESI status applies to your resubmission window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing primary institute/IC must be done prior to resubmission unless arranged
rubrics_metrics.description: You could have changed institutes, but the time to do that was prior to resubmission (ie, submit and request new IC, having made arrangements with appropriate PO to accept the application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want an application considered primarily by a different IC, make arrangements with that IC’s PO before resubmitting. Post-submission institute changes are limited and require coordination.
